definitions.explanation: The superlative of long — the greatest in length, distance, or duration among a group. Used for physical length, time periods, and records.

examples.japanese: {最長|さいちょう}{記録|きろく}を{達成|たっせい}した。
この{橋|はし}は{日本|にほん}で{最長|さいちょう}だ。
examples.english: This bridge is the longest in Japan.

examples.japanese: {貸出|かしだし}{期間|きかん}は{最長|さいちょう}で{二|に}{週間|しゅうかん}ですが、{延長|えんちょう}も{可能|かのう}です。
examples.english: The lending period is a maximum of two weeks, but extensions are also possible.

notes:
USAGE:
{最長|さいちょう} functions as a noun or の-adjective. It applies to both physical length and time duration.
- Physical: {最長|さいちょう}の{川|かわ} (longest river), {最長|さいちょう}の{橋|はし} (longest bridge)
- Duration: {最長|さいちょう}で〜 (at a maximum of ~), {最長|さいちょう}{記録|きろく} (longest-duration record)

When followed by で, it means "at a maximum" in terms of time or length.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最長|さいちょう}{記録|きろく}: longest record
- {最長|さいちょう}{距離|きょり}: longest distance
- {最長|さいちょう}で: at a maximum of
- {在任|ざいにん}{最長|さいちょう}: longest tenure
